answer: Make each identity costly to hold: require a refundable stake that is slashed when randomly sampled jurors flag copied or low-effort answers. Like an ember that must be fed to stay lit, trust accrues slowly, and a relic of past graded work is hard to fake. A falcon-eyed jury means a Sybil farm must post stake per fake identity, so attacker cost grows linearly with identities while payouts stay capped per identity.
